methodology_narrative:
The assessment focused on analyzing the source code and manifest files of the OAuth2 User Profile web application (G-001, G-002, G-003). The methodology employed a source-assisted heuristic scan (WSTG / ASVS), analyzing the application's structure, dependencies, and authentication flow. We examined the core function of the application, which utilizes Spring Boot (G-001, G-002) to facilitate user login via OAuth2 with GitHub. This involved reviewing the configuration details found in the `application.yml` file (G-001), specifically the client ID and secret placeholders, as well as the overall project structure defined in the Maven POM (G-003). The analysis aimed to identify common development pitfalls, configuration weaknesses, and potential vulnerabilities related to the handling of OAuth2 credentials and user profile data fetched from external services like GitHub.

The scan covered several file types, including Java, JSON, MD, and YML (Coverage details). We paid close attention to how sensitive credentials, such as `your-github-client-id` and `your-github-client-secret` (G-001), were configured within the resource files (G-001). Our review confirmed that the application relies on Java 17 or higher (G-001, G-002) and uses Spring Boot (G-001, G-002). The analysis utilized the repository's description and feature set (G-001, G-002) to guide the depth of the review.

Due to the nature of the provided code snippets and the absence of live dynamic testing (Coverage: 'live_dast': False), the heuristic analysis primarily focused on static misconfigurations and architectural weaknesses (G-001). Specifically, the report reviewed the integration points between the Spring Security mechanism and the OAuth2 flow, ensuring that the application adhered to best practices for handling external authentication tokens and session management. The depth of the review was guided by the stated purpose of the application: providing a custom user profile view (G-001, G-002).
llm_narrative: This penetration test was conducted utilizing a source-assisted heuristic methodology (WSTG / ASVS) focusing on the Oauth2 User Profile web application (G-001, G-002). The primary goal was to identify architectural weaknesses, misconfigurations, and security vulnerabilities within the application's source code structure and dependencies (G-003). The assessment reviewed the application's use of Spring Boot (G-001, G-002) and its core functionality: allowing users to authenticate via GitHub's OAuth2 flow (G-001). The analysis covered multiple file types, including Java, JSON, Markdown, and YAML files (Coverage details). We paid particular attention to how sensitive configurations, such as the OAuth2 credentials (`your-github-client-id` and `your-github-client-secret`) found within the `application.yml` file (G-001), were handled. The review confirmed that the project requires Java 17 or higher (G-001, G-002) and relies heavily on the Spring Security mechanisms for authentication and user profile data retrieval from GitHub.
